figures.caption: Stage 1 (0.1 s) diagnostics for all 120 trials, including observations before failure. Small symbols: one trial statistic; connected large symbols: mean across ten trials per method/width; bars: sample SD (ddof=1), not confidence intervals. Successful normal solves only, using fresh geometry and saved planning covariance. (a) Within-trial P05 of phi-d_col (d_col=0.05 mm). (b) Fraction with phi-d_col < -1 micrometre. (c) Fraction with R>0.1+1e-6 conditional on phi>d_min=0.1 mm and valid separated features. (d) Within-trial P05 of the same chance-budget residual epsilon-R, with epsilon=0.1 and zero as the constraint boundary. R is the same local Gaussian/Boole surrogate on both controllers, not measured collision probability, and may exceed one. Domain exits are reported separately. Observation lengths differ; paired common-time sensitivity is supplementary.

Stage 10 (1 s) diagnostics for all 120 trials, including observations before failure. Small symbols: one trial statistic; connected large symbols: arithmetic mean across ten trials per method/width; bars: sample SD (ddof=1), not confidence intervals. Within each trial, successful normal solves are evaluated using freshly recomputed geometry and their saved planning covariance. (a) P05 of phi-d_col, d_col=0.05 mm. (b) Fraction with phi-d_col < -1 micrometre. (c) Fraction with R>0.1+1e-6, conditional on phi>d_min=0.1 mm and a valid separated feature model. (d) P05 of the common chance-budget residual epsilon-R, epsilon=0.1 and R=sum_i p_i; zero is the constraint boundary. R is a common local Gaussian/Boole surrogate evaluated on both controllers, not a measured collision probability, and may exceed one. Domain exits are excluded only from (c,d) and are reported separately in the coverage figure/tables. Failure-trial observation lengths differ; see paired common-time sensitivity. Stage 10 is a predicted horizon state, not an executed next pose.

Stage-1 trial statistics; mean +/- sample SD over ten trials per width/method, with individual trial symbols. (a,b) Same frozen nominal features at the solved candidate: p_selected<=0.1-1e-6 and max p_other>0.1+1e-6. Equivalent selected feature aliases are excluded. (b) Also requires the offending feature to lie within 0.5 mm of the selected feature at the nominal state. Rates use valid nominal separated-domain candidates. (c) Within-trial P95 of |h_fresh-h_frozen|; (d) P95 of |h_frozen-h_affine|, using the same SF diagnostic row on both trajectories, in mm. These are local-model discrepancies; (d) is covariance-margin linearization error, not a covariance dynamics defect. Refer to manifest for finite-row eligibility. The MF path is evaluated counterfactually with the same SF diagnostic; these are not native MF solver residuals.

Trial points and mean +/- sample SD across ten trials. (a) Stage-1 successful normal candidates with phi<=d_min=0.1 mm. (b) Disjunction: phi<=d_min OR (valid separated model and R>epsilon+1e-6); this is a condition frequency, not an imputed probability. (c) Minimum actual signed PSDF, including failed trials; repeated terminal stops do not change the minimum. (d) QP fallback episodes per 100 solver attempts; stage-0 Guard stops are excluded. Rates do not remove trajectory/exposure confounding.

Consecutive-cycle nominal residual changes conditional on a canonical selected-feature change. Both SF standardized residual and MF quantile residual are evaluated at the same states on each source trajectory; both MF endpoints must use the ordinary inverse-CDF branch (no extension or clipping). Each dot is the trial mean absolute change; bars are sample SD across trials with eligible events, never zero-imputed trials. Only adjacent valid, active separated-domain cycles are used; missing/fallback gaps are not bridged. Pose and covariance vary across cycles: these are observed temporal changes, not discontinuity estimates. The controlled finite-offset boundary figure isolates local boundary sensitivity. All-pair, non-switch, and ordinary inverse-CDF branch results and sample counts are retained in the CSV tables.

Stage-1 paired differences, MF minus SF, with ten same-seed pairs per width. Each dot is one pair and bars are mean +/- sample SD across pairs. Full observed uses each complete available trajectory. Common time prefix truncates both members at the earlier last successful normal solve time. This checks exposure sensitivity; matching elapsed time does not match pose, covariance, controls, or causal treatment.

The raw common multi-feature risk sum R is evaluated at each successful normal candidate with valid separated geometry. Each point is a within-trial mean (left) or within-trial sample SD (right); large symbols and bars are the across-trial mean and sample SD of those statistics. All observed trials are included, including pre-termination segments of failed trials. R may exceed one and is not an empirical collision probability. Extreme saved planning-covariance states remain included; robust P05 chance-budget margin summaries in the main figure and the outlier audit complement these moment statistics. The two levels of SD describe temporal dispersion within a trial and dispersion between trials, respectively; neither is a confidence interval.

Stage-1 common-risk sensitivity at identical saved candidate poses and a common valid separated domain. Left: covariance stored in the optimizer solution. Right: covariance recomputed by the archived nonlinear one-step dynamics from the reset initial covariance and applied input. Each small symbol is one trial statistic; large symbols and bars are the mean and sample SD across ten trials. R is a local Gaussian/Boole surrogate in both cases, not measured collision probability. Candidate poses and actual trial outcomes are not changed or re-simulated. A documented log-Cholesky outlier strongly affects mean raw R, while its effect on threshold-exceedance frequency is much smaller. Both versions remain in the data; no outlier is deleted. Trial exposure varies, including only two valid candidates in the shortest 130 mm MF trial.

Stage-1 switching-boundary sensitivity across all widths and both source controllers, without selecting a route segment or successful trials. Two endpoints lie 10 micrometres on each side of each localized canonical-feature boundary in the body-motion metric ||delta_xy||+r|delta_theta|. The original left-cycle body-frame planning covariance is fixed for both endpoints and both evaluator functions. No extrapolation past the observed nominal segment is used. Both endpoints must be separated, valid and MF-active, with ordinary inverse-CDF branches; clipping and linear-extension events are excluded from this primary figure. Each small symbol is one trial mean absolute finite-offset change; large symbols and bars are the mean and sample SD across trials with eligible events. n is the number of such trials, not independent boundary events. Top: standardized SF and MF residual changes in common quantile units. Bottom: changes of epsilon-p_selected and epsilon-R in percentage points, using the same event set. R is a local Boole surrogate sum, not measured collision probability. Five and fifty micrometre offsets, all active branches, P95/RMS, and all excluded-event counts are retained in the tables. These are local finite-offset sensitivities, not mathematical discontinuity limits or proof of improved closed-loop completion.
